experiment: 138M BAIR video-WM: KDA-layer-count Pareto (quality vs rollout efficiency)
method: attention surgery (init KDA from pretrained softmax q/k/v/o) + cross-layer Block-AttnRes(groups 4); re-finetune 40k on 18.8k BAIR-aux
recipe: standard bair-64-act-free.sh: effective batch 64 (bs32/gpu x2), lr 1e-4 cosine, max_grad_norm 1.0, segment_length 16, context_length 1, wd 0.01, llama_attn_drop 0.1, embed_no_wd; frozen bair-64 tokenizer
eval_setting: gen_times 1 (fair, same for all), 256 BAIR-aux test
data_caveat: 18,778 train (subset ~44% of full ~43k; Berkeley server throttle). Internal comparison unaffected; absolute FVD not comparable to paper full-data 60.8 (also gen100 vs our gen1).

K0_sdpa_baseline.desc: paper 60.8 model itself (SDPA full attention), eval-only

rollout_decode_peak_mem_GB.note: peak GPU mem for autoregressive decode; SDPA layers grow KV cache O(N), KDA layers O(1) state. Latency column omitted (KDA decode path unreliable in this harness).

takeaway: Linearizing the temporal attention (75% or 100%) retains near-parity FVD (+2 to +3.4% vs SDPA baseline) while cutting long-rollout decode memory 35-46% at N=32768 (saving grows with KDA-layer-count x rollout length). Token-level eval_loss degrades more (2.14->2.58) than perceptual/FVD quality, i.e. AttnRes+KDA preserves video quality despite higher per-token perplexity. On this data/budget all-KDA already near-parity, so it dominates the 75% hybrid here; the hybrid is the safer choice when a larger quality gap must be closed.
